(countable, more broadly) A set of conventions for writing a language, including norms of spelling, capitalization, emphasis, hyphenation, punctuation, and word breaks.
(uncountable) The aspect of language study concerned with letters and their sequences in words; the study of spelling.
(uncountable) Correct spelling according to established usage; also (obsolete) pronunciation according to the spelling of a word.

(countable, architecture) A form of projection used to represent three-dimensional objects in two dimensions, in which all the projection lines are orthogonal or perpendicular to the projection plane; an orthographic projection, especially when used to draw an elevation, vertical projection, etc.,…
(transitive, rare, archaic) To spell (words) or write (text) according to established usage.
(genetics) Any of two or more homologous gene sequences found in different species related by linear descent.
(genetics, of genes or sequences) Exhibiting orthology; having been separated by a speciation event. Usually while retaining the same function.
(genetics) One of two or more homologous gene sequences found in different species.
Relating to the theory that human health, including mental illness, depends upon chemical deficiencies and can be cured with vitamins etc.
(functional analysis, geometry, linear algebra) Of a set of vectors, both orthogonal and normalized.
(functional analysis, geometry, linear algebra) Of a linear transformation: that preserves both angles and lengths.
Of or relating to orthopedics.
(medicine) The branch of medicine that deals with the prevention or correction of disorders of the bones and associated muscles and joints.
(medicine) A surgeon who specializes in orthopedics.
(inorganic chemistry) Any salt or ester of orthophosphoric acid; an ordinary phosphate
(chemistry) Describing the ordinary form of phosphoric acid and its derivatives
An aerial photograph that has been geometrically corrected (orthorectified) such that the scale of the photograph is uniform, meaning that the photo can be considered equivalent to a map.
Correctness of practice or action in regard to religion and especially religious ritual, particularly in juxtaposition to "correct doctrine", or "correct belief" (that is, "orthodoxy").

Right belief combined with right practice, with the emphasis on the latter, often in Latin American liberation theology, contrasting with an orthodoxy seen as insufficiently interested in the practical and political content of faith.
Any of very many four-winged insects, of the order Orthoptera, such as grasshoppers, crickets and locusts
Relating to orthoptics, the study and treatment of muscular irregularities of the eye.
(geometry) The isoptic whose given angle is a right angle.
(mineralogy) Any pyroxene that forms orthorhombic crystals.
(psychology) A fixation with healthy or righteous eating.
(crystallography) Having three unequal axes at right angles.
(medicine) A type of brace which either prevents or assists movement of a limb or the spine.
Relating to orthostasis or orthostatism.
(archaeology) Relating to an orthostat.
Of or pertaining to orthotics.
(typography) Of Greek typography: having an upright form, distinct from the cursive and chancery types.
An orthopedic appliance designed to support, straighten or improve the functioning of a body part; an orthosis.
(medicine) The design, manufacture and installation of orthopedic appliances to support, straighten or improve the function of a body part
A person who makes or fits orthotic devices.
(anatomy) in the normal position
(botany) Growing vertically, either upwards or downwards.
(engineering) Having material properties that differ along three mutually orthogonal twofold axes of rotational symmetry.

The greater short-toed lark (Calandrella brachydactyla).

A motor vehicle restricted to non-road venues. A vehicle not allowed on public roadways.
A motor vehicle designed to be able to travel across terrain without road surfaces.

A white wine from that town.

Resembling the totalitarian political methods decried in the works of writer George Orwell, particularly in the dystopian novel Nineteen Eighty-Four; characterized by use of misleading terminology, propaganda, censorship, surveillance and repression.
Resembling, or having to do with, George Orwell, and especially his novel 1984.
Any of several antelopes, of the genus Oryx, native to Africa, which have long, straight horns
A form of pasta the size and shape of grains of rice or barley; often used in soups.
